mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -27.3% to -4.1% over three weeks) reflects a monotonic recovery trajectory. This trend continuation mechanism predicts RETAIL_REC will remain positive relative to the baseline over the next four weeks, driving the target direction upward.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved by 23.2 percentage points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the last 28 days, or weekly RETAIL_REC declines for two consecutive weeks in the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -9.0% to +11.3% over three weeks) signals normalized essential-goods shopping behavior. This normalization reduces substitution pressure on retail-recreation spending, allowing discretionary mobility to recover as confidence in routine activity resumes.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase relative to baseline when GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5% for two consecutive weeks, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts below 0% in the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility deficit (currently -13.1%) constrains retail-recreation access. If TRANSIT remains below -10% over the next four weeks, suppressed commuting capacity will limit retail footfall, preventing RETAIL_REC from recovering above the recent baseline mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -13.1% in t-0w, improving from -38.4% three weeks prior
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above the last 28-day mean despite TRANSIT remaining below -10%, or TRANSIT recovers above -5% within the first two weeks of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surge (72.1% in t-1w, 68.3% in t-0w) indicates outdoor-activity substitution for indoor retail-recreation. This substitution effect will persist if PARKS remains elevated, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth as consumers allocate discretionary time to parks rather than retail venues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above +60% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above the last 28-day mean while PARKS remains above +60%, or PARKS falls below +50% and RETAIL_REC does not subsequently increase within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of WORKPLACES recovery (from -41.7% to -19.7%) and TRANSIT improvement (from -38.4% to -13.1%) signals restoration of commuting infrastructure. When both proxies improve simultaneously, commuter-driven retail footfall accelerates, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by >5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 22 points over three weeks; TRANSIT improved 25.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvement, or either proxy reverses by >3 percentage points in the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility decline (from +4.7% to +1.4% over three weeks) indicates reduced stay-at-home compliance, signaling policy relaxation or voluntary behavioral shift. This regime transition enables retail-recreation venues to operate at higher capacity, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +2% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +1.4% in t-0w, lowest in the snapshot
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above +3% and RETAIL_REC does not increase, or RETAIL_REC remains below the last 28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL staying below +2%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September timing (t-0w = 2021-09-15) in Melbourne coincides with spring onset and school-term resumption. Seasonal demand for retail-recreation activity increases as families resume out-of-home routines, producing a positive RETAIL_REC shift over the next four weeks independent of current mobility levels.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2021-09-15, spring season onset in Southern Hemisphere
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean, or weekly RETAIL_REC declines in three or more weeks of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility remains suppressed (currently -19.7%) while PARKS mobility remains elevated (68.3%), consumers substitute work-commute retail stops with leisure-time retail visits concentrated in park-adjacent and recreational retail zones. This substitution pattern will sustain RETAIL_REC near current levels over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -15% AND PARKS above +60% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -19.7%, PARKS at 68.3%, RETAIL_REC at -4.1%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines below -10% when WORKPLACES remains below -15% and PARKS above +60%, or WORKPLACES recovers above -10% without a corresponding RETAIL_REC increase within one week.
